title: Family Passes, waiting limits and the player screens that go with them
changes: A family host sees a Family Passes card (also before check-in opens) and can approve or decline the people who ask through the family link, until 15 minutes before the game begins
A request that nobody answers lapses after 30 minutes with a polite message, and the person can ask again
New games follow these rules from 2026-10-29 23:36:07 UTC (the value APPROVAL_RULES_FROM_MS = 1793316967027); every game made before that moment behaves exactly as in 1.7.1

title: The player screens in two looks
changes: The page a player sees has two looks, Retro and Modern, with a calm layout where the ticket is the only rich part
The first screen says who invites you and what to type. In a two-ticket game you choose which ticket you are playing and the other one is greyed
A crossed number keeps its number and gets a thin cross. The end screen starts with a thank-you and the Share and WhatsApp buttons

title: One clean top menu, the new logo and fixes from user feedback
changes: The top menu has six items: How it works, Free demo game, Guide, Brochure, Refer & earn, Log in. The same menu is on the front page and on every information page. On a phone it opens from a Menu button

The Corporate Tambola badge (red ticket badge, CORPORATE above Tambola) is now the logo everywhere: the website, the app icon on phones, the share picture, e-mails, game reports, the brochure and the organizer manual
Pricing, the free assistant, the video and WhatsApp us are no longer in the top menu. They are still on the front page, in the footer and on the Contact page
Every page footer now shows the version and the release date and time, for example: Version 1.7.0, released 29 Oct 2026, 15:30 IST
Clearer fairness wording (no one knows the next number) and a shorter footer that names who owns the site and who collects payments
Fixes from user feedback: clearer messages when a Co-host link is for another game, and a reminder e-mail for a game still in draft

title: Game names, plain wording
changes: Every game name on the front page now has the small CORPORATE line above it, with the game picture, and Lucky Draw joins the row of six games
The label above the headline reads: For HR teams and managers

Plainer words in the pages, e-mails and console: personal links instead of private links. The legal pages say close group game and protected record in place of the old wording; the meaning is unchanged
The games bar says Close group online engagement and its first item opens home.corporatetambola.com

title: A fresher, friendlier front page
changes: The front page has a warmer, more colourful look, a Choose your game row with all six games, and a short list of what you can count on
A big Try a free game with 10 people button, and our phone number and e-mail right at the top
Different layouts for phone and laptop. The game screens are unchanged

title: Front page headline in plain English
changes: The front page headline now reads: This week, which teams will you engage with a close group online Housie?

title: The game has its own address: housie.corporatetambola.com
changes: Corporate Tambola now lives at housie.corporatetambola.com. Links in e-mails, share texts, reports and PDFs use the new address
The games bar at the top of every page points Tambola to the new address and Corporate Games to home.corporatetambola.com
The front page now opens with a question: which team will you engage this week

title: Rehearsal guests, listening count, our logo in the PDF, shorter claims
changes: When you start a rehearsal you now choose who is invited: the same guests as your game, the last rehearsal's guests, nobody yet, or a few guests you tick from your game's list
Your Co-hosts get a new link for each rehearsal (shown to you when you start it). Hosts need nothing new
Game details now shows about how many phones are listening right now (pages that are in front). It is a count only: no names or numbers are kept, and it adds only a few small writes an hour
Our logo now also appears in the PDF report, next to the customer's logo
A claim now travels as a short line of text instead of a longer message. Older open pages keep working

title: Language dropdown (English for now)
changes: A small language dropdown at the top right of every screen. English is the only language for now. The choice is remembered in this browser and can be changed at any time, even in the middle of a game. All claim notices now come from one list of messages, so a second language is one more table later
The dropdown sits outside the part of the page that redraws every second, so it never closes by itself, and it is never near the gold Claim buttons

title: Branded reports and e-mails
changes: The game report e-mail now carries our logo and the customer's logo and colour at the top, simple summary tiles (game started, completed, players, numbers called, prizes awarded, claims), the prizes table, every claim and what came of it (including Prize already taken), what happened during the game (pauses and changes with who and when), a button to open the complete report, and a More games from Corporate Tambola block. Its subject is Your game report is ready: <game name>, <date>, and it has a plain-text part with the same facts. Only ticket numbers are in the e-mail

The PDF report has the customer's colour in its top band and new sections: at a glance, prizes, every claim and the event log, and More games. The game log page and its text download carry the same header, summary and More games block
A rehearsal's report and game log say REHEARSAL GAME n at the top, like its other pages and e-mails
The customer's logo is served as a picture for e-mails (never anything that can run); all games are listed from one place so the web addresses are easy to change later

title: Three free rehearsals for every paid game
changes: Every paid game now has three free rehearsals, one after the other, under the Publish step. Each rehearsal is a real run of the game with its own game code, its own links, tickets and check-in, so nothing from a rehearsal can touch the real game. The cards are grey with First publish your game and pay until the game is published and paid

Every page, share text and e-mail of a rehearsal starts with Game ID, REHEARSAL GAME n and This link and this game are for rehearsal only. The real game has a different link and a different game. E-mail subjects start REHEARSAL GAME n (practice only). A finished rehearsal shows a calm page that offers the real game
The same people can use all four runs (rehearsal 1, 2, 3 and the real game) with a separate link, ticket and check-in each time. Rehearsals are not counted as games and cost nothing
The Organizer's console now shows a calm pop-up when someone claims a prize (ticket number only)

title: Phones ask in turns, so a very big game stays smooth
changes: Every phone now asks the game whether anything changed at its own moment, decided by its ticket number: 8 turns in small games, up to 64 in very big ones, so thousands of phones no longer ask all at once. Big games (over 2,000 players) ask every 3 seconds, over 5,000 every 4 seconds. A claim still reaches every phone within about 3 seconds in a game of 2,000 and about 5 seconds in a game of 10,000

After a claim, each phone reads the new list after a short wait of its own (up to half a second, up to a second in big games), also by ticket number. The person who pressed Claim is never made to wait
If a phone gets no answer for a few seconds it says Reconnecting, calmly, and the line goes away by itself. A phone that is not in front (hidden tab) asks nothing
The words of the claim notices now come from one list of messages stored in the app (a code and its text), the base for a second language later

title: A crowd joining at once is cheaper for the database
changes: Joining writes everything in one database transaction instead of seven (the seat, the person rows, the two per-address counters and the consent record), so a crowd of people opening the link at the same moment costs the database much less. The records kept are exactly the same
The seat and claim list and the public control file are answered from the edge cache for a few seconds, so a very large game does not slow down when everybody asks at once
The Are you sure question of a grey Claim button closes by itself when a prize becomes ready to claim, so it can never sit on top of the gold CLAIM buttons

title: Claim buttons, claim timer, fast claim notice
changes: Claiming is clearer: when a player has a prize to claim, three gold CLAIM buttons appear together, at the top inside the alert (You have won the Top line. Click CLAIM to claim.), at the bottom and beside the prize. They are one claim: pressing any of them, or pressing twice, sends one claim. The rest of the time the buttons beside the prizes are grey, and pressing one first asks (it would count as a wrong claim, a Bogey) with Cancel and Submit

A small claim timer on the gold buttons (Claim in the next 11 s, down to 0) where the game calls the numbers itself. For that player only, the usual Next number countdown is hidden while the timer shows and returns at the next number. No timer when a Host calls the numbers. The timer is a nudge: the claim rule is unchanged and the game's clock decides

Everyone hears of a claim within a few seconds: a tiny signal (a few digits, asked every 2 seconds only while the page is in front) moves whenever someone claims, and then the phones, the Organizer's board and the big screen show a calm pop-up with the ticket number. No names or numbers are shown

Plain words for the start and the calling in step 2: Auto start / Manual start, The game calls the numbers / I call the numbers, and one summary line (Your game: starts at 10:30 when you press Start. You call the numbers.) repeated at the Publish step
At Publish, every prize with no name is listed (4 prizes have no name: ... Winners will get nothing. Go back and name them, or press Publish anyway.)

The game log and the report now explain a late-but-in-time claim: Prize already taken: this claim came at number N, after the prize was already awarded at number M. The rule is written there too: everyone who claims before the next number is called wins that prize together; if there are more winners than prizes the organizer or host decides how to share; Unlucky is awarded automatically

title: Manual play has no fixed gap
changes: One speed (a new number every 12 seconds) is for games where the game calls the numbers itself, whether it starts by itself or you press Start. When a Host presses for each number there is no fixed gap: the Host sets the pace, and nothing in the game says otherwise

In a game where a Host calls the numbers, no screen counts down to the next number any more (the player's phone, the big screen, the Organizer's board and the console): they say The host calls the numbers, or Waiting for the host

A Host game can be made, saved and copied with any speed value: the 12 second rule never refuses or changes it. The report says The host called the numbers (no fixed gap), and the list of changes no longer shows a speed change for a Host game

The claim rule is unchanged and checked with a Host pressing at uneven moments: a claim counts only before the Host's next press takes effect, decided by the game's clock; while the game is paused it stays open; after the last number it stays open for 12 seconds
The help texts, the AI helper and the rules now say when the game calls the numbers itself, a new number comes every 12 seconds

A tap is never lost: the player page, the Organizer's board and the big screen no longer redraw while a finger or mouse button is down (it is redrawn right after), nor while text is selected, and scroll position and typed text stay where they were. A Claim press or a number tap can no longer vanish because the screen refreshed at that moment
After the game has ended the player screen says it once: no Checking with the organizer banner, no second end message, and the number panel says The game is over instead of Find it on your ticket

title: One plain story for everybody
changes: Every screen (player's phone, big screen, Organizer, Host, Co-host) says in one plain sentence what is happening now and what to do, in the same words: before publishing, waiting for payment, waiting for the start, countdown, running, paused, finished early, finished, never started, cancelled
A clear counter everywhere: the number just called, one short line such as 31 of 90 called · 59 left, and the last 5 numbers called; players never see the full list or a board of all 90 numbers
Game details for the Organizer and Hosts during the game: status, numbers called, people joined and waiting, prizes won so far with ticket number and time, pauses, warnings

After the game the Organizer and the Hosts can open or download the game log (start and end time, how it ended, people, every prize with ticket number and time, pauses, changes with who, the report e-mail, every number called with its time); it has ticket numbers only and is kept for 365 days; a Co-host can read it too (ticket numbers only, never names or numbers)
Pause is harder to press by accident: it asks Are you sure? and needs a tick; when it is on, a big banner shows on every screen

Claiming: when a player completes a prize an alert and a big Claim button appear at once and vanish when the next number is announced; a claim pressed after the next number is refused kindly and records nothing, decided by the game's clock in all four modes

The player page is two designs: the phone (one column, the ticket most prominent, a fixed Claim button) and the laptop (two columns); the prizes show what is still to win and who won what by ticket number; Sneha's three rules sit under the ticket

One speed for new games: a new number every 12 seconds (90 numbers take about 18 minutes, about 36 with two tickets; with claims 30 to 60 minutes); games already published with another speed keep working
The prize for both tickets of one player is called the Super Bumper House: it is won when all 30 numbers of the player's two tickets together have been called
A Lucky Draw the organizer chose is listed with the other prizes on the players' page, the organizer's and the Host's screens and in the game log
A small, quiet countdown, Next number in 7s, beside the counter on the players' page and the organizer's and Host's screens, taken from the game's own schedule; it makes no sound

The organizer's board screen shows the live game on one page: the whole log newest first, claims as they come (accepted, wrong or too late), people, the average gap between numbers called by the game and by hand, the story line, the quiet timer and the controls (Start, Pause with a confirm, Resume, Add 30 minutes, Next number) that only the Organizer and Hosts see

The organizer's log is written as plain proof lines with the exact time (Number 12 announced 8:15:04 pm · 31 of 90 called · 59 left) and a check line at the top says whether any number was missed; the game log says the same

Everybody sees calm pop-ups when a ticket claims a prize (Ticket 214 has claimed Top Line. Checking now), whether it was correct, and that the prize is no longer available; they use public ticket numbers only and they arrive as fast as the phone refreshes the list of claims
When a phone comes back to the front after a call or another app, it asks for the right time at once and says how long the person was away; a short tip suggests Do Not Disturb during the game

Every page is checked in a real browser at phone, tablet and laptop widths, and sideways on a phone: the ticket is wide enough to read, every number fits inside its square, nothing is cut off and nothing needs sideways scrolling; the laptop page uses the full width

Start, Resume, Add 30 more minutes and Next number on the board screen now ask Are you sure? first (like Pause); a Co-host sees the board panels without the buttons; the live log and the claims list show every line; the saved game log also lists every claim (accepted, wrong, too late) by ticket number

New games take one speed only, a new number every 12 seconds, also when made through the API or by the AI; older games keep their speed and a copy of a game gets 12; a claim on the last number of a game closes one gap after it is announced

title: Press Start at any size
changes: Pressing Start now works for games of any size; a Host or the Organizer calling every number stays for games of up to 1,000 people

Very large games (above 2,000 people) have their own slow checking profile and a longer countdown after Start, about 3 to 4 minutes, so every phone hears Start before the first number and they all begin together; players see the countdown
In those games Pause and End are not available (they would reach phones too late to be fair); Start is the one control, and the console says so in plain words

title: Game-day clarity
changes: A big Number board button and the numbers called so far (the latest highlighted, with how many of 90) now sit at the very top of the Organizer's and Host's game screen; the Co-host gets the board button

A big PAUSED banner on the console, every player's phone and the big screen says who paused, since when and until when, with a Resume button on the console; Pause now asks Are you sure? Numbers stop for everybody
A clear ending in plain words for players, the big screen, the console and the report e-mail: All 90 numbers were called, or All prizes were awarded after N numbers

A new question in How will it play: When every prize is won, keep calling until all 90 numbers, or end the game; new games start with keep calling; games made before keep the old rule until the Organizer chooses
Pause, resume, extend, end and Start are written in the What changed list with who did them

title: Four game modes
changes: Two plain questions in the console: "How does it start?" (by itself at the time, or I press Start) and "Who calls the numbers?" (the game does, or I do): together they make four modes

A big Start button on Game day for the Organizer and every Host; it stays off until the start time and says why, and if nobody presses it the game waits (it is never started by the system) and the console says: Press Start, or change the start time
Start is signed like Pause and Next number, so every phone, the big screen and the Hosts' screens begin together, about 40 seconds after the press; the numbers cannot be known or chosen before Start

After publishing, the Organizer or a Host can still change the start time, the way the game starts and runs, and every other setting until the game starts, with the same links; phones and screens follow at once
A plain list of what changed, who changed it and when, for the Organizer and the Host and kept in the game record, with no player data in it
A game that was published but not paid no longer blocks a new game: the draft limit counts only drafts that were never published
Players can choose the ticket look, Retro (default) or Modern; the Retro ticket is the traditional coloured card with a red cross over crossed numbers
Players see: the start time before it, waiting for the host to begin the game at it, then a countdown after Start

title: The owner can make one game free
changes: From the private owner console the owner can make one specific game free (Rs 0): the game is given a pack of its own size and published at no charge, once, with the reason written on the owner access log
Works like a discount voucher for that one game; nobody else can do it

title: A free pack is used when you press Publish again
changes: If Publish was pressed before a free demo link was opened, the game stayed waiting for payment even after the link gave a free pack; pressing Publish again now uses the free pack and the game publishes at Rs 0
Found live with a real prospect whose game had been held for payment before she opened her link

title: One-time Rs 0 prospect links made from the owner console
changes: The owner can make a Rs 0 demo link for a prospect (100 people by default, ends after 7 days by default): it gives one account one free game, once
The owner can switch a link off or on at any time; a link that is switched off or past its date says so in plain words
Made and switched only with its own key from the private owner console

title: A demo link now works when you are taken straight back into your game
changes: If you opened a free demo link while the console took you straight back into a game you had already made, the free game was not given and the game still asked for payment; the link is now used first, and the console tells you to press Publish
Found with a real prospect who made a 250 game first and then opened the 250 link

title: A private numbers call for the owner console
changes: A read-only call that gives the owner the counts of games made, started and completed, players, organizers and the latest version
It opens only with its own key; every other caller gets the same plain not-found answer, and each try is written to the owner access log
It never returns a mobile number or any player data

title: A join that gets no answer is asked again by itself
changes: If a phone sends its join and no answer comes back (slow link, busy moment), the page asks again by itself after a short random wait instead of showing a failure
Joining is safe to repeat: the same person always gets the same ticket
Found on the real site in the 250 and 500 person test games

title: A Host's AI work link and an unaccepted Co-host can do less
changes: A Host's narrow AI work link can no longer register control keys or file pause, stop or erase requests (it can still read the public pause file)
A Co-host who has not accepted the role terms can no longer start a payment with credit
Numbers written with 00 in front of the country code (0091 98765 43210, 0065 9123 4567) keep working with the new country-code check
Found by the 9,841-scenario permission tests run on the live 1.3.1

title: Unknown country codes are refused with a plain sentence
changes: A mobile number typed with a country code that does not exist (for example +999) is now refused when joining and in people lists, with the same plain sentence the page shows: We do not know that country code. Please pick your country from the list.
Found by the 1,520-scenario journey tests on the live 1.3.0; every other scenario passed

title: Simpler organizer console, the organizer has the final say on prizes, and safety fixes
changes: The organizer console is simpler: the options for more prizes above 5 (lines and other prizes) or above 10 (Full House and the two-ticket Full House), the choice of more than one round and the question about people who finish together are hidden (nothing is removed, they can be switched back on); a plain line tells the organizer the game works like a real housie

After the game the organizer sees the result the software worked out and has the final say: a Change winner button lets them give a prize to one of the tickets that claimed it, or to nobody; every change is kept with who made it and when

When people finish together on the same number they take the next prize positions one after the other, so 3 prizes and 2 correct claims give one prize each and leave one open (no question to the organizer)
A manual game whose Host has not opened the game-day page now shows Waiting for the host and does not start by itself

Safety: a result or a game over reported by a phone now counts only from the phone that holds that ticket (made-up ticket numbers can no longer end a game or name a winner); the organizer's erase-all is refused while the game is being played; a Co-host must accept the role terms before paying or using credit; a size raised while the payment window was open can no longer end above the pack that was paid for

title: Join and organizer fixes found by the 10,000-case scenario tests
changes: A phone number typed with a space-saving format is read correctly: +44 (0)7911 123456, (+44) 7911 123456, numbers pasted with invisible marks, typographic dashes or Arabic/Devanagari digits, and a US number typed as 1 555 ... all become the right number

Joining: an Indian mobile number that cannot exist (first digit not 6, 7, 8 or 9) is refused on join the same way it is in a list; a game that could not begin because payment is not complete seats nobody; a person the organizer already admitted is no longer asked the (wrong) employee ID again and left waiting; a ticket without its phone proof is not handed back
A country list with the mobile number field (India first), mandatory and optional marks per mode, and the name shown as the organizer gave it

Organizer: plain sentences instead of 'check the details', an invalid 'who can join' is refused, the game size cannot go below the people already on the list; the people list exports foreign numbers exactly

Safety: posts to the control address no longer use up the day's write budget unless they are signed (a pause or stop still works on a day the budget is spent); the daily write guard now charges a join what it really writes; held demo-pass secrets are swept after 2 hours

Roles: a Co-host and an invited guest now follow the same rules in every list and approval route; the waiting-room approval no longer leaves a person inside a declined request; invited places are kept in open games
The Privacy page lists the country choice kept on the phone

title: Idiot-proof console and players, beacon relay, demo link hold
changes: All 79 confirmed audit problems where a person could be stuck or confused were fixed across the ten organizer steps, the Host and Co-host pages and the player pages: refusals are shown beside the button with what to do, nothing is silently lost, buttons say Saving and work once, instructions match what the page does, plain words instead of codes

The game no longer needs the beacon's own servers to be reachable: our own server relays the public random-number service as the last route, and a blocked route is asked last for a while (a company firewall no longer stalls a game at 0 of 90 numbers)
A demo link's free game is granted whichever browser finishes the sign-in (kept with the e-mail address on the server)
The pause file all phones ask for is answered once per place per second and shared: far fewer database reads in big manual games
The 1.1.x fixes (logo upload, Delete a draft, waiting list banner, no links from a draft) are part of this release

title: Demo pass links
changes: Owner tool: a secret link (zc.html?pass=...) gives the account that opens it ONE free game (Rs 0) of up to 100 or 250 people, one to one, for a prospect the owner chose. Nothing is shown to the public; the size list and prices are unchanged. Only hashes of the links are kept in the code; each link works once

title: Console: busy Save, waiting list, no links on drafts
changes: Save and continue says Saving, cannot be pressed twice, and moves on at once instead of waiting for a slow refresh
A request that never answers no longer freezes the page (it gives up after 40 seconds with a plain message)
Add a Host or Co-host pressed twice no longer makes two people or sends two e-mails
People waiting to be let in are shown as a banner on every step, with a button to the waiting list
A game that is not published shows Do not send links yet; the per-person send buttons and Play now say Publish first
What belongs to one game (a cancelled note, a payment link, a message) no longer follows the person into another game

title: Logo upload hotfix, delete a draft
changes: HOTFIX: choosing a company logo with the real file dialog made the console throw an error while redrawing, so no button of that step worked afterwards (a prospect could not get past step 4). Fixed; the redraw never touches a file box now
Your games: an unpublished draft has a Delete (two taps). The 10-draft limit can no longer trap anyone, and the message says how to free a place
A note such as Draft deleted no longer follows the person into the next game

title: Step 4 never blocks a person
changes: A prospect could not get past step 4: a logo without a company name was refused and the reason was shown at the top of the step. Now the game is always saved: a name without a colour gets the first colour; a logo or colour without a name is simply not used yet, with a calm note
Any reason a Save is refused is also shown right above the Save button, in a red box

title: Sign-in tries, big-game claims, waiting-room words
changes: Sign-in code tries are counted before the code is compared, so wrong codes sent all at once still stop at five
In big games a full page of claims is no longer followed by a later Bogey: phones cannot skip claims
The waiting room says the common link, a personal link or the game link instead of internal codes
One network address may now open 600 new places a minute and 20,000 a day (was 200 and 1,500): a whole office shares one address, so a crowd joining together is no longer turned away

title: Review fixes: Host AI key, cash edit, people list
changes: Security: the 24-hour Host AI-link key can no longer finish a Host setup and turn itself into a lasting Host key
Editing the amount or currency of a saved cash prize is now saved
Step 6 shows one Play the game yourself block (the second copy had dead buttons and duplicate ids)
My people list loads every page even when removed rows exist
Smart Placement switched on: the Function runs next to the database, so a join (about 26 database calls) is no longer slowed by a far-away edge

title: Employees-only and ID check kept on re-save
changes: Console: after a reload the form shows the saved employees-only, employee-ID check and tie rule, so saving step 2 or 3 no longer wipes them (found by the code review; regression test added)

title: Second browser and kept typing
changes: The organizer signed in on a second browser or phone can add that browser's own signing key, so Next number and Pause work there
Unsaved typing and ticks in the console survive the page refreshing itself; pressing a button starts from the saved state

title: Game day line, owner-only version history
changes: Game day step: a line says the Organizer / Host logs into the game and controls it
Owner-only version history page and release list (not visible to the public)

title: First market-ready release
changes: Cash prize option with currency chips (INR default) and amount
Notice under video and audio links: we do not save them, we play them from the link
Staff-list consent box hidden and sent automatically; clause 11.4A in the Terms
Professional data-handling text in step 10
AI welcome e-mail switched off at sign-up
Daily write guard raised for the paid Cloudflare plan

title: Manual games in every browser
changes: The organizer control key now works in browsers without WebCrypto Ed25519 (pure-JS fallback), so Host-mode games run on the Host's own schedule in Safari-type browsers

title: Six-sigma test programme fixes
changes: Employees-only and employee-ID settings are no longer lost when a later step is saved
Organizer e-mail at the top right, help text for who the game is for
Click-only live tests on corporatetambola.com in Chrome, Chromium and WebKit

title: Verify and employee-ID release
changes: Employee ID and mobile verification options
All-products test and go-live audit

title: Guided errors
changes: Every mistake gets a polite explanation, exact steps and a button to the right place
Public promises corrected (brochure prices, partner repeat rate, Razorpay address)

title: Payment testing and Corporate Games bar
changes: Payment Testing page (real Rs 1 / US$ 1 payment that buys nothing)
Corporate Games bar on every public page

title: Simpler step 2 and people lists
changes: No prices in step 2, own number of players, clearer wording
People lists, personal and common links, waiting room

title: Data deletion and brand moments
changes: Participant data crypto-shredded at 23 hours, report link closes at 22 hours
Brand moments: opening, three during, closing

title: AI work link and privacy links
changes: Short AI work link
Privacy Policy link on the join page

title: First build
changes: Game engine, organizer console, payments on the Worker (Razorpay), GST invoices
